newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-TIGANA TAKES IT ONE MATCH AT A TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TIGANA TAKES IT ONE MATCH AT A TIME.

text.p: Monaco coach Jean Tigana kept his players focused on Thursday on their French Cup match at second division Laval, avoiding the temptation to look ahead to next week's key league clash with a bloodied Paris Saint-Germain.

"We want to win on all fronts," Tigana said. "We came back well (from the holidays) with victory at Le Mans (in the League Cup), now we need continuity and to keep up our good state of mind for the battles to come."
Monaco travel to Laval for Friday's only match in the first round of the French Cup which continues with another 31 games spread over the weekend.
General manager Henri Bianchetti said: "We don't want to think of PSG yet, but one thing is certain, we are playing to win in all our matches."

PSG, who saw Monaco overtake them and open a four-point lead in the first division before the winter break, went from bad to worse with a 6-1 home defeat by Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup on Wednesday.
Monaco host PSG on January 26 looking to pull further away from their chief rivals for the league title.
Midfielder Ali Benarbia said: "We must not focus on PSG yet. It's true this defeat is very negative for them ... but we can't think in terms of the poor results of our rivals.
"Our first concern is Laval and the French Cup."
Monaco, who last won the French Cup in 1991, are nearly at full strength with Belgian playmaker Enzo Scifo back after missing most of the first half of the season with a broken toe.
They also welcome back defender Emmanuel Petit from injury, while striker Victor Ikpeba is back after missing the game at Le Mans because of international duty with Nigeria.
But Scottish midfielder John Collins is nursing a thigh injury and has been left out of the squad.
Brazilian striker Anderson, who hit a hat-trick in Sunday's 3-1 win at Le Mans, said: "At Laval, unlike Le Mans, it will be a more physical than technical match and we must win.
"We also want to go far in this competition ... let's forget PSG for the moment."
At the weekend, holders Auxerre are away to minor league side Vervins, while PSG play third division Besancon with their confidence rock bottom after the roasting by Juventus.
